text: An employee whose wages have been delayed or not paid can file a claim before the Authority appointed under the Payment of Wages Act. The claim must generally be filed within 12 months of the wages becoming due. The Authority can order payment of the wages due plus compensation.

A dismissal, discharge, retrenchment, or termination of an individual workman is treated as an industrial dispute even if no other workman or union is party to it, allowing the individual to raise the matter before the Labour Court or Conciliation Officer.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
text: Every workplace employing 10 or more employees must constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to receive and inquire into complaints of sexual harassment. A complaint must generally be filed within 3 months of the incident, extendable by the Committee.

act: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
text: If an employer fails to deposit PF contributions, the amount can be recovered as arrears of land revenue. Employees can also complain to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner (RPFC) for non-deposit of PF or ESI contributions.

A consumer complaint regarding defective goods, deficient service, unfair trade practice, or overcharging can be filed before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Complaints can also be filed online via the National Consumer Helpline / e-daakhil portal.

Unfair trade practice includes false representation of goods or services, misleading advertisements, and deceptive practices. A consumer harmed by such practices can seek compensation and corrective orders from the Consumer Commission.

A homebuyer facing delayed possession, or where a builder has not delivered promised amenities, can file a complaint with the State Real Estate Regulatory Authority against the promoter/builder for compensation or refund with interest.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
text: A woman facing domestic violence (physical, emotional, verbal, economic, or sexual abuse) from a family member can file an application before a Magistrate seeking protection orders, residence orders, and monetary relief, with assistance from a Protection Officer.

Following or repeatedly contacting a woman despite her clear disinterest, or monitoring her use of the internet/email/electronic communication, constitutes stalking and is a criminal offence that can be reported to the police.

Capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of a person's private area without consent violates privacy under the IT Act. Non-consensual sharing of morphed or private photos can also be reported to the Cyber Crime Cell or via cybercrime.gov.in.

Giving or taking dowry is a punishable offence. Harassment for dowry can also be reported under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita's cruelty-by-husband-or-relatives provision, alongside relief under the Domestic Violence Act.

Section 9 allows a spouse to seek restitution of conjugal rights; Section 13 lists grounds for divorce (cruelty, desertion, adultery, etc.). Either party may approach the Family Court depending on the relief sought.

act: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (formerly CrPC Section 125)
text: A wife, children, or aged parents unable to maintain themselves can seek a maintenance order against a person with sufficient means who has neglected or refused to maintain them, filed before a Magistrate.

A District Court may appoint a guardian for a minor's person or property if it is satisfied that this is for the welfare of the child, considering the child's age, sex, wishes, and relationship with the proposed guardian.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 / CARA Regulations
text: Legal adoption in India is processed through the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) portal, requiring registration, home study, and court/District Magistrate confirmation of the adoption order.

Where one co-owner of property transfers their share, the transferee acquires the rights of that co-owner, including the right to joint possession, subject to the equities between the other co-owners.

act: State Rent Control Acts (varies by state)
text: A landlord seeking to evict a tenant, or a tenant seeking return of a security deposit after lease termination, must generally proceed before the Rent Controller or Civil Court as per the applicable state Rent Control Act.

Free legal aid is available to women, children, persons with disabilities, SC/ST members, industrial workmen, victims of trafficking, persons in custody, and those with annual income below the state-notified limit, through the District/State Legal Services Authority.

Lok Adalats can settle pending or pre-litigation disputes through conciliation, particularly suited for compoundable civil and criminal matters, motor accident claims, and matrimonial disputes where parties are open to compromise.
A person injured in a motor vehicle accident, or the legal heirs of a person killed, can file a compensation claim before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) against the vehicle owner/insurer.
